purpose: The judgment layer for running a business VoIP reseller's recurring book after cutover: designing the support model the per-seat fee actually funds, triaging faults by layer and driving carrier escalations with evidence, keeping E911 dispatchable-location records continuously current, reading churn signals early enough to run honest fix-first saves and clean port-out exits, holding billing, contract and renewal conduct to disclosure-first standards, and growing seats, features and adjacent services only where an account's own record evidences the need.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a local one-person or small-crew VoIP reseller running a book of small-business accounts - dental practices, trucking offices, restaurants, motels, professional offices - on an upstream platform or carrier the operator resells rather than owns

accounts arrive from the deployment discipline already cut over, with numbers ported, devices working, and E911 configured at deployment time; this KB governs everything that happens to the account after that handoff

every specific price, wholesale rate, commission, tax figure, churn rate, and uptime number lives in the operator's own contracts, upstream agreements, and book records; this KB describes only the mechanisms that generate those numbers and the verification path for each

content is educational and operational knowledge for running the business, never personalized legal, tax, financial, or insurance advice; regulatory obligations are named by class with a verify-current-rules flag
exclusions: channel model selection (agent versus reseller versus white-label), niche picking and segment pain profiles, offer packaging, per-seat pricing design, and competitive positioning - the sibling channel-economics KB owns these; this KB inherits the sold offer and the written support promise as given inputs

needs assessment, phone and softphone selection, number porting-in execution, network readiness and QoS engineering, failover architecture design, initial E911 configuration, cutover planning, and user training - the sibling deployment KB owns these; this KB operates and maintains what deployment built, including keeping E911 records current and activating already-designed failover during outages

stating any specific commission, wholesale or retail price, tax rate, churn percentage, account multiple, or uptime figure as fact - economics appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands verified against the operator's own book and agreements

asserting the operator's USF-class contribution, telecom-tax, or regulatory registration position - those obligations are named by class, differ by channel model, and are routed to a qualified telecom attorney or tax professional in the operator's jurisdiction
guaranteed-uptime or savings claims without a verified basis such as the upstream provider's published SLA or the customer's documented current bill

asserting the current text of E911 rules - the Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class of obligations is treated as a standing hard flag whose current requirements must be verified, never assumed and never skipped
consumer and residential VoIP, carrier-scale network engineering, and building or operating the softswitch platform itself

competency_questions.question: What does running the recurring stage of a VoIP reseller business actually consist of, and what record must deployment hand over before support can own an account?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECURRING_BASE_FRAME names the four jobs of the book (keep, support, bill, grow) and the per-account margin mechanism, and SERVICE_INTAKE_HANDOFF lists the as-built record support refuses to operate without

competency_questions.question: What support does the monthly per-seat fee include, what is billable project work, and how are hours and response bands kept honest to what the operator can staff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPORT_MODEL_DESIGN draws the bundled-versus-billable line with examples and ties every stated hour and response band to the support promise actually sold

competency_questions.question: How is a voice-quality or dead-phone complaint isolated to device, customer LAN, ISP, or platform before anything is escalated upstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAULT_TRIAGE_LADDER gives the layer order, the symptom signatures that point at each layer, and the evidence captured before escalation

competency_questions.question: What does a carrier or platform escalation ticket need to move on the first pass, and what is the customer told while the fix sits in the platform's hands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRIER_ESCALATION_PATH lists the escalation packet contents and the truthful customer-communication stance that neither hides behind the carrier nor promises times the operator does not control

competency_questions.question: How is a platform-wide outage handled - detection, blast-radius check, failover activation, communication cadence, and credits afterward?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTAGE_RESPONSE_PROTOCOL sequences detection, verification, failover activation, honest proactive communication, and post-incident credits applied from recorded terms

competency_questions.question: What E911 duties survive deployment, and which everyday events force a dispatchable-location record update before a ticket may close?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: E911_RECORD_MAINTENANCE names the Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class of continuing obligations, the triggering events (moves, adds, relocations, remote users), the no-close-without-record rule, and the verify-current-requirements flag

competency_questions.question: Which signals mark an account as churn risk before the cancellation call, and what save motion is honest when a flag opens?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_HEALTH_SIGNALS lists the leading indicators including the quiet-after-complaint pattern, and CHURN_SAVE_PLAYBOOK orders the save motion fix-first, right-size second, price as mechanism, never obstruction

competency_questions.question: What must offboarding include when a customer ports out, and why is the port never obstructed even mid-dispute?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORT_OUT_OFFBOARDING states that the numbers belong to the customer, lists the prompt-porting-data duty and the offboarding checklist, and separates unpaid-balance collection from the port itself

competency_questions.question: How is the monthly invoice kept accurate, and how does tax and fee treatment differ between agent-style and reseller-style channel positions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BILLING_INTEGRITY requires per-cycle seat reconciliation, plain-language line items, no invented fee lines, and routes USF-class and telecom-tax treatment to professional verification per the operator's channel model

competency_questions.question: How are contract terms, auto-renew windows, and SLA promises tracked, and how is a renewal conducted without evergreen traps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRACT_SLA_REGISTER defines the dated commercial register bounded by the upstream published SLA, and HONEST_RENEWAL_MOTION requires proactive notice ahead of the auto-renew window with seats re-verified and pricing explained as mechanism

competency_questions.question: How do periodic account reviews surface seat growth, feature adoption, and adjacent-service cross-sell without turning the review into a sales ambush?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CADENCE builds the agenda from the account's own record, SEAT_EXPANSION_MOTION and FEATURE_ADOPTION_UPSELL ground every offer in an observed need, and CROSS_SELL_BOUNDARY limits adjacency to what the operator can genuinely deliver or transparently broker

competency_questions.question: How is per-account and book-level margin understood as a mechanism, and how is support labor kept from silently eroding it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MRR_BOOK_ECONOMICS decomposes margin and MRR motion into named inputs each traced to a book record, and SUPPORT_LOAD_CONTROL converts repeat-cause analysis into permanent fixes, self-service, or an honest re-price conversation

competency_questions.question: How is the book tiered so attention lands where it earns, and when does the upstream platform relationship itself become the book's biggest risk?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIER_SEGMENTATION tiers on revenue, strategic weight, health, and load while holding service floors uniform, and PLATFORM_RELATIONSHIP_WATCH keeps the incident log, wholesale terms, and a credible migration option current

competency_questions.question: What does the periodic whole-book review decide account by account, and what definition-of-done closes it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_REVIEW_GATE composes health flags, renewal windows, expansion findings, load outliers, and the platform stance into dated decisions with owners, and states the per-account definition-of-done or documented exception

glossary.definition: The sum of every account's monthly per-seat and feature charges; the asset the recurring stage protects and grows, whose motion decomposes into new accounts, expansion, contraction, and churn.
One billed user or extension of the phone service - a dental front desk, a dispatcher, a motel front office line; the unit both the monthly invoice and the E911 record set are counted in.

The street address plus the in-building detail (floor, suite, room) that must be conveyed with a 911 call under the RAY BAUM class of rules; every seat move or remote user makes an existing record wrong until it is updated.

The deployment handoff document support operates from: call flows and auto-attendant trees as actually configured, device inventory, admin credentials, port completion evidence, registered E911 locations, and the written support promise.

The written boundary between work the monthly fee includes (routine adds, moves, changes, resets, minor call-flow tweaks) and work quoted as a project (relocations, call-flow rebuilds, new-site build-outs); the line that stops support scope creep.

The evidence bundle an upstream ticket needs to move on the first pass: timestamped failing-call examples with calling and called numbers, affected extensions and DIDs, the local layers already ruled out, and site WAN details.
A router feature that rewrites SIP packets in transit; a notorious cause of one-way audio and registration drops, and therefore one of the first suspects when triage reaches the customer-LAN layer.

The contract-defined period before an automatic renewal during which either side may give notice; missing it commits the customer silently, which is why the register tracks it and the honest-renewal motion opens before it.

The discipline of promising customers no more availability than the upstream provider's published SLA supports, with the operator's own response-time commitments recorded separately as personal promises the operator can actually staff.

Correcting an account's seats and features to match its real usage in either direction - including downward at the operator's own MRR expense - because an oversubscribed account is churn on a delay timer.

nodes.definition: Fix what the post-cutover stage of a business VoIP reseller actually is: a book of small accounts - dental front desks, trucking dispatch lines, restaurant host stands, motel front offices - each paying monthly per-seat service with a support promise attached, where the asset is the book itself, not any single install. Per-account margin is a mechanism: contracted per-seat retail minus platform wholesale minus the support labor the account consumes, with the real numbers living in the operator's own agreements and time records. The recurring stage has four jobs that everything downstream serves: keep accounts (churn prevention and honest saves), support them (triage, escalation, outage response), bill them honestly (invoice, contract, and renewal hygiene), and grow them (seats, features, and adjacent services grounded in observed need). The frame also fixes the boundary: the offer and its pricing were designed upstream by the channel-economics discipline, and the system being supported was built by the deployment discipline; this stage operates and compounds what those stages hand over.

included: the four jobs of the book: keep, support, bill, grow
per-account margin as a mechanism with named inputs
the boundary against the sales-stage and deployment-stage disciplines
excluded: channel model choice and offer design
deployment and cutover work
any specific margin or churn figure asserted as fact

pros.claim: Naming the book as the asset reorients a small operator from install-chasing to retention economics
pros.example: choosing to spend Thursday afternoon killing a motel's recurring dropped-call fault rather than quoting one more new install, because the account's continuing service revenue outweighs a single setup fee

cons.claim: Book-first framing over-applied starves new-account acquisition and shrinks the very base being protected
cons.example: a quarter spent entirely on account reviews and ticket hygiene while the install pipeline the sibling disciplines feed goes empty

failure_modes: treating recurring service as dead time between installs so tickets queue and churn compounds quietly
framing support as pure cost and starving it until the book erodes faster than new installs replace it
acceptance_tests: the operating frame states the four jobs, the margin mechanism with each input's source record, and the two sibling-stage boundaries in writing
revisit_triggers: the operator's own book behaves differently than the frame assumes - churn concentrating where the frame says it should not
the business adds a second crew member or a second platform, changing what one operator can hold in their head

base.update_signal: the operator's actual margins, churn pattern, or crew size contradict the frame's assumptions

nodes.definition: Refuse to own an account in support until the deployment discipline hands over a complete as-built service record, because every missing piece is paid for later in rediscovery time on a live fault. The intake record holds: call flows and auto-attendant trees as actually configured including time conditions and holiday rules, device inventory with models and physical locations, admin portal credentials held somewhere other than the installer's head, evidence the ports completed and which numbers ride which trunks, the E911 dispatchable-location entries as registered at cutover, the written support promise the offer sold, and named customer contacts with an after-hours escalation path. Gaps found at intake go back to deployment while the install is still warm; gaps found six months later during a Saturday outage are archaeology under fire.

included: the as-built record contents
the intake gap check while the install is warm
credential and contact custody
excluded: performing the deployment work itself
designing what the record documents

pros.claim: A complete as-built record collapses first-ticket resolution time
pros.example: fixing a restaurant's complaint that the Saturday greeting still plays on Monday in minutes by reading the documented time-condition rules instead of reverse-engineering the auto-attendant live

cons.claim: Intake documentation is unpaid time at exactly the moment the crew wants to move to the next install
cons.example: skipping the as-built after a Friday cutover, then losing an hour re-deriving ring groups during Tuesday's first fault call

failure_modes: accepting an account with no as-built so every future fault begins with archaeology
credentials or port records existing only in the installer's memory when a fault hits during their vacation
acceptance_tests: each new account's intake record contains call flows, devices, credentials, port evidence, registered E911 entries, the support promise, and named contacts, or the gap is logged back to deployment with a date
revisit_triggers: a fault reveals the as-built no longer matches reality after undocumented changes
the deployment discipline changes its handoff format

base.update_signal: intake gaps recur on the same fields, showing the handoff checklist needs restructuring

nodes.definition: Design the support model the per-seat fee actually funds and write it down before the first out-of-scope request sets a precedent. First-line bundled work: routine adds, moves and changes within stated limits, voicemail and PIN resets, greeting and minor call-flow tweaks, warranty device swaps, and how-do-I questions. Billable project work: office relocations, call-flow redesigns, new-site build-outs, integrations. Hours, channels, and response-time bands are stated only at levels a one-person or small-crew shop can truly staff - a same-business-day response promise honestly kept beats a 24/7 promise quietly broken - and the whole charter must match the support promise the offer sold, never silently exceed or undercut it. The charter allows documented exceptions with an expiry, so generosity to a valued account is a decision, not a drift.

included: the bundled-versus-billable line with examples
staffable hours, channels, and response bands
documented exceptions with expiry
excluded: what support promise to sell - the sales-stage discipline owns that
fault triage mechanics

pros.claim: A written bundled line stops support scope creep before it compounds
pros.example: a restaurant asking for a full seasonal-menu IVR rebuild gets a small project quote instead of the work silently absorbed into the monthly fee

cons.claim: A rigidly applied line reads as nickel-and-diming to a loyal account
cons.example: invoicing a ten-minute greeting change for the dental office that refers new patients invites resentment far exceeding the invoice

failure_modes: promising around-the-clock response a small shop cannot staff, then breaking it visibly
letting every request into the bundle until per-seat margin quietly goes negative
the charter contradicting the support promise the customer was actually sold
acceptance_tests: the charter lists bundled work, billable work with trigger examples, staffed hours and response bands, and reconciles line by line against the sold support promise
revisit_triggers: exception requests cluster on one work type, signaling the line is drawn in the wrong place
crew size or platform tooling changes what is staffable

base.update_signal: repeated exceptions or a change in the sold support promise force the charter to be redrawn

nodes.definition: Run first-line VoIP triage as a layer ladder worked in order - device (phone, headset, cabling, power), customer LAN and Wi-Fi (switch, PoE budget, DHCP and VLAN, SIP ALG on the router), ISP and WAN (bandwidth saturation, modem or circuit flaps), then platform and carrier - because each layer has symptom signatures that point at it: one-way audio suggests NAT or SIP ALG interference, choppy or robotic audio suggests jitter and packet loss on the local network or a saturated uplink, a single dead phone suggests device or port, and simultaneous no-registration across sites suggests platform or WAN. Before any escalation, capture evidence: timestamped failing-call examples with calling and called numbers, affected extensions, what each lower layer test showed, and quality statistics where the platform portal exposes them. The ladder exists to stop two expensive mistakes: blaming the carrier for the customer's own congested Wi-Fi, and rebooting phones during a genuine platform outage.

included: the four-layer order and symptom signatures
evidence capture before escalation
the platform-status short-circuit check
excluded: network redesign or QoS engineering - the deployment discipline owns the fix at that depth
the upstream ticket mechanics

pros.claim: Layered triage prevents wasted upstream tickets and preserves escalation credibility
pros.example: catching a restaurant's choppy audio as its own Wi-Fi drowned by POS tablets and guest devices before opening a carrier ticket destined for a no-trouble-found reply

cons.claim: Walking the full ladder is slow when the true fault is a platform outage
cons.example: having a motel clerk reboot handsets one by one while the platform status page already shows a regional registration failure

failure_modes: defaulting to blame-the-carrier and burning credibility with both the platform and the customer
skipping evidence capture so the eventual escalation ping-pongs for days
never checking the platform status page first and triaging a known outage
acceptance_tests: the triage runbook maps symptom signatures to layers, opens with the platform-status check, and its evidence checklist is completed before any ticket escalates
revisit_triggers: a fault class repeatedly lands at the wrong layer, showing a signature mapping is wrong
the platform exposes new diagnostics that should join the evidence checklist

base.update_signal: resolution logs show a symptom signature mapping mis-routing faults, or new device classes change the ladder

nodes.definition: Drive escalations to the platform or carrier the operator resells without owning the network: an upstream ticket moves on the first pass only when it carries the escalation packet - at least three timestamped failing-call examples with calling and called numbers, the affected DIDs and extensions, the local layers already ruled out with what each test showed, and the site's WAN details - with severity set honestly and the reference number, owner, and follow-up cadence logged. The customer-facing half is equally disciplined: tell the truthful split of what sits in the operator's hands versus the platform's, give the platform's stated timeline only as the platform's statement, and never invent a fix time the operator does not control - while also never hiding behind the carrier, because the customer bought the service from the operator and the relationship debt lands there.

included: escalation packet contents
severity honesty and follow-up cadence
the truthful customer-communication stance during upstream work
excluded: local-layer triage
platform-wide outage handling, which has its own protocol

pros.claim: Evidence-complete tickets skip the retest loop that doubles resolution time
pros.example: an intermittent inbound-failure ticket accepted on first pass because it includes three timestamped failed calls and shows the LAN and WAN layers already ruled out

cons.claim: The operator carries the customer relationship while lacking control of the fix
cons.example: a trucking office losing dispatch calls hears that the platform is still working on it for a second day, and blames the reseller it pays rather than the platform it never met

failure_modes: escalating without the packet so the ticket bounces back as no-trouble-found
quoting the customer a hard fix time the platform never committed to
letting an upstream ticket idle with no follow-up cadence until the customer calls first
acceptance_tests: every upstream ticket in the log carries the full escalation packet, a severity honestly matched to impact, and dated follow-ups at the stated cadence
revisit_triggers: the platform changes its ticketing intake or severity definitions
tickets with complete packets still bounce, signaling the platform's intake expectations shifted

base.update_signal: upstream ticket outcomes show the packet or cadence no longer moves tickets on the first pass

nodes.definition: Handle a platform-wide or site-wide outage as a practiced routine, not an improvisation: detect early from the platform status page, monitoring alerts, and the tell-tale of several accounts calling at once; verify the blast radius - one site's WAN versus the whole book - before saying anything; activate the failover routing deployment already designed, such as forwarding front-desk numbers to cell phones or an answering service, operating the design rather than inventing it mid-incident; communicate proactively at a stated cadence with honest status - what is known, what is not, no minimizing and no invented restoration times - so customers hear it from the operator before they discover a silent phone; and afterward write a short post-incident note, apply any SLA credits due from the recorded contract terms without waiting to be asked, and file the incident into the platform log that informs the stay-or-migrate stance.

included: detection and blast-radius verification
failover activation and honest cadence communication
post-incident notes and unprompted credits
excluded: designing the failover architecture - deployment owns that
the platform relationship decision the incident log feeds

pros.claim: Proactive outage communication converts a bad platform day into a trust deposit for the reseller
pros.example: motel front desks get a text within minutes saying inbound calls are failing platform-wide and their lines are being forwarded to cell, before a single guest-facing phone is discovered dead

cons.claim: Honest mass notification amplifies awareness of failures some accounts never felt
cons.example: an office closed on Monday learns of Sunday night's outage only from the notice and requests a credit for an impact it never experienced

failure_modes: waiting for each customer to discover the outage and call in
minimizing with just-a-blip language while the platform status page says otherwise
forgetting the failover designs exist and leaving business numbers ringing dead for hours
acceptance_tests: the outage runbook names detection sources, the blast-radius check, per-account failover activation steps, the communication cadence with honest-status wording, and the credit procedure driven from recorded terms
after any incident, the post-incident note and the credit application exist without a customer having asked
revisit_triggers: an incident review finds the cadence, failover steps, or detection sources failed in practice
the platform changes its status-page or notification behavior

base.update_signal: a live incident exposes a gap between the runbook and what actually worked under pressure

nodes.definition: Treat E911 as a continuing service obligation, never a deployment checkbox: the Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class of rules - direct 911 dialing without prefixes, on-site notification when 911 is dialed, and a dispatchable location conveyed with the call - binds the service for as long as it runs, so the records configured at cutover start going stale the first time the customer rearranges anything. Every seat move, suite or floor change, office relocation, new remote or softphone user, and number change triggers re-verification and update of the dispatchable-location records before the ticket that caused it may close - the no-close-without-record rule is absolute. Because the rule class evolves and platform provisioning mechanics differ, current requirements are verified against the rules in force and the platform's E911 workflow on a stated cadence and at every relocation, never assumed from last year's compliance. This is the hard flag of the whole subdomain: a wrong location record surfaces exactly once, during someone's worst moment.

included: the continuing-obligation framing of the Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class
trigger events and the no-close-without-record rule
the verify-current-requirements cadence
excluded: initial E911 configuration at deployment
asserting the current legal text - the flag is verify, never assume

pros.claim: Coupling the E911 record action to every move-add-change ticket keeps compliance current by construction
pros.example: a dental practice moving two suites down the hall has its new dispatchable location registered and test-verified inside the move ticket itself, not remembered weeks later

cons.claim: Strict E911 gating slows routine work and can read as bureaucracy to the customer
cons.example: a same-day seat add for a motel waits on location-record confirmation before the ticket closes, and the clerk asks why a working phone is not finished

failure_modes: treating deployment-time E911 setup as permanent while the customer quietly rearranges offices
softphone users roaming on laptops with a registered address they left months ago
assuming requirements are unchanged instead of verifying the rules currently in force
acceptance_tests: every move, add, or change ticket carries an explicit E911 record action - updated, verified unchanged, or escalated - before closure
current E911 requirements are re-verified against the rules in force on the stated cadence and at every relocation, with the check dated
revisit_triggers: any change to the E911 rule class or the platform's E911 provisioning workflow
an audit finds a seat whose registered location does not match where the device actually sits
an account adds remote or softphone users

base.update_signal: the E911 rule class, enforcement posture, or platform provisioning mechanics change

nodes.definition: Read churn risk from data the operator already holds, months before any cancellation notice: ticket frequency rising or the same fault recurring unresolved; a quality complaint that suddenly goes quiet, because silence after complaints usually means the customer is shopping, not satisfied; seat counts drifting down at invoice reconciliation; payment slipping from on-time to late; an ownership change or a new office manager who inherited no loyalty; a competitor's quote mentioned in passing; paid features nobody uses. Each signal becomes a dated health flag with an owner and a next action - a flag with no owner rots into hindsight. The flags are not verdicts: a seasonal seat drop at a motel is rhythm, not defection, so every flag is read against the account's own baseline. Health flags are the shared input that drives saves, review agendas, and tiering.

included: the leading-indicator catalog with the quiet-after-complaint pattern
dated flags with owner and next action
baseline reading to separate rhythm from risk
excluded: the save motion itself
tier assignment mechanics

pros.claim: The quiet-after-complaint signal catches the most dangerous churn while it is still saveable
pros.example: a restaurant that stopped reporting its choppy-audio problem gets a proactive visit and turns out to be evaluating a competitor's bundled POS-plus-phones pitch

cons.claim: Signal-chasing misreads ordinary noise as churn risk and wastes save effort
cons.example: treating a motel's every-winter seat reduction as defection and running an awkward save call on a perfectly loyal account

failure_modes: first learning of churn at the cancellation notice because nothing was flagged
flags logged without owner or date so nobody acts until hindsight
reading every fluctuation as risk and numbing the operator to real flags
acceptance_tests: the signal catalog is written with per-signal examples, and every open flag carries a date, an owner, and a next action
revisit_triggers: an account churns with no flag ever raised - the catalog missed its signal
exit findings from departed accounts contradict which signals actually predicted loss
billing or ticket tooling changes what data is observable

base.update_signal: a churned account's post-mortem shows a signal the catalog lacked or one it overweights

nodes.definition: Run saves in honesty order. First, fix the actual fault: most small-business VoIP churn traces to an unresolved quality problem or service friction, not price, so a save that opens with a discount usually buys a few months of the same resentment. Second, right-size - including downward: drop seats and features the account does not use even though it cuts MRR, because an honestly smaller account outlives an oversubscribed one that feels overcharged. Third, price moves only as mechanism: re-quote against current wholesale and honest margin, never a theatrical manager's-discount invented for the call. Never retention-by-obstruction: no hidden cancellation paths, no surprise fees, no games with the port process. And know when to let go - an account whose needs the operator genuinely cannot serve gets a clean referral out, which costs one account and protects the reputation that feeds the rest of the book.

included: the fix-first, right-size, price-as-mechanism order
the no-obstruction rule
the let-go decision and clean referral
excluded: offboarding mechanics once the customer decides to leave
signal detection

pros.claim: Fix-first saves are durable where discount-first saves merely defer the loss
pros.example: a trucking office ready to cancel over dropped dispatch calls stays for years after the real cause - a saturated DSL uplink - is fixed with an LTE backup, where a discount alone would only have delayed the same cancellation

cons.claim: Right-sizing down and referring out sacrifice near-term revenue by design
cons.example: cutting a motel from twelve seats to seven at review trims MRR the same month the operator's own equipment loan payment lands

failure_modes: leading with a discount that masks the unfixed fault, paying twice - the margin and the eventual churn
treating every save as winnable and burning weeks on an account already signed elsewhere
sliding into obstruction tactics that convert one loss into a reputation problem
acceptance_tests: each save attempt is logged with the fault status at open, the motion order actually run, and the outcome, so the playbook can be audited against its own rules
revisit_triggers: save outcomes show discounts being reached before faults are confirmed fixed
a pattern of unwinnable saves suggests the let-go criteria trigger too late

base.update_signal: save-log outcomes contradict the motion order - fixes not holding or right-sizing accelerating churn

nodes.definition: When a customer leaves, the exit is a service act and the numbers are the customer's - a business's phone number is its crown jewel, and it was never the operator's to hold hostage. Provide accurate porting data promptly: account numbers, the records the winning carrier's port request needs, any port-out PIN. Never obstruct or slow-walk a port, never invent exit fees the signed agreement does not contain, and never condition the port on settling a billing dispute - unpaid balances are pursued as ordinary collections on a separate track, and the porting-rules class that governs carrier changes treats obstruction as complaint-worthy conduct, so verify current porting obligations rather than testing them. The offboarding checklist closes the account completely: final invoice reconciled, hardware ownership resolved per contract for owned versus rented devices, voicemail and recording exports offered where the platform allows, E911 records closed out, credentials revoked, and the account marked closed in the register. In a small town, the departing office manager's next employer is the operator's next prospect; clean exits are marketing.

included: prompt porting-data duty and the no-obstruction rule
the full offboarding checklist
separating collections from the port
excluded: the save motion that precedes a decided exit
porting-in execution for new accounts - deployment territory

pros.claim: Clean exits reflow into the referral pipeline that feeds a local book
pros.example: an office manager who left over a merger recommends the operator at her next employer specifically because the port-out was handled in days without games

cons.claim: Prompt, helpful port-outs make leaving frictionless and occasionally speed a loss a save might still have caught
cons.example: releasing porting data the same afternoon forecloses the week a scheduled fix-first save call still needed

failure_modes: sitting on a port request hoping the customer cools off, converting one loss into a complaint and a story that circulates
charging exit or record fees never contracted
leaving E911 records, billing, and credentials open after service ends
acceptance_tests: every exit shows porting data provided promptly and dated, no uncontracted fee, collections handled on a separate track, and the offboarding checklist fully closed including E911 record closure and credential revocation
revisit_triggers: the porting-rules class or the platform's port-out workflow changes
an exit post-mortem finds a checklist item that stayed open

base.update_signal: porting obligations or platform port-out mechanics change, or an exit generates a complaint

nodes.definition: Keep the monthly invoice a document the customer never has to fight: seat counts reconciled to reality every cycle so nobody pays for seats removed months ago, adds and changes landing on the very next invoice as plain-language line items, and service-failure credits applied from the recorded contract terms without being begged for. Tax and fee treatment follows the operator's channel model and is verified, never guessed: under agent-style arrangements the provider typically bills the customer and carries the remittance duties, while reseller-style arrangements put the operator in the billing chain with USF-class contribution and telecom-tax obligations whose current treatment must be confirmed with a telecom-savvy accountant or attorney in the operator's jurisdiction. Pass-through fees are labeled as exactly what they are; inventing official-sounding recovery lines that mimic taxes but pad margin is the invoice equivalent of cramming, and a single discovered padded line can cost more trust than the line ever earned.

included: per-cycle seat reconciliation and plain-language line items
channel-model-dependent tax treatment routed to professional verification
unprompted credits and honest fee labeling
excluded: setting the price levels - the sales-stage discipline designed them
asserting any specific tax rate or USF-class figure

pros.claim: Reconciled invoices remove the single most preventable churn trigger
pros.example: a dental office that shrank from eight operatory seats to six sees the decrease on the very next invoice, converting a would-be grievance into visible proof of honesty

cons.claim: Per-cycle reconciliation costs real hours every month forever
cons.example: an evening walking twenty invoices against seat records is an evening not spent on billable project work

failure_modes: billing stale seat counts until the customer audits and every past invoice becomes suspect
inventing fee lines that look like taxes
guessing the USF-class or telecom-tax position instead of verifying it professionally per the channel model
acceptance_tests: each cycle's invoices reconcile to current seat and feature records with the reconciliation dated
every fee line is contracted, a labeled true pass-through, or removed
the tax and USF-class treatment on the invoice matches the operator's professionally verified channel-model position
revisit_triggers: the operator's channel model changes, changing who bills and who remits
a billing dispute reveals a reconciliation gap
tax or USF-class treatment guidance is updated by the operator's professional

base.update_signal: a channel-model change, a professional's updated tax guidance, or a dispute pattern in the billing log

nodes.definition: Maintain one dated register of every account's commercial facts so renewals, credits, and entitlement questions are answered from a record instead of memory: term start and end, the auto-renew clause and its notice window, contracted per-seat rates and the mechanics under which they may change, hardware ownership status per device class, and the SLA actually promised. For a reseller the availability promise is bounded by the upstream provider's published SLA - no uptime figure appears anywhere the upstream document does not support - while the operator's own response-time commitments are recorded separately as personal promises the operator staffs. The register is what makes honesty operational: it drives renewal timing before notice windows close, computes outage credits from real terms, and answers what-am-I-entitled-to without improvisation. A register that decays into stale amendments is worse than none, because it answers confidently and wrong.

included: term, notice-window, rate-mechanics, and hardware-ownership tracking
SLA bounded by the upstream published SLA with operator promises recorded separately
the register as the single source for renewals and credits
excluded: drafting contract terms - the sales-stage discipline shapes the offer
the renewal conversation itself

pros.claim: The register turns renewal season from ambush into schedule
pros.example: a ninety-day forward look shows three motel contracts entering their notice windows next quarter, each queued for a review before anything auto-renews

cons.claim: Register discipline is unglamorous overhead that silently decays without a cadence
cons.example: two years in, half the entries miss un-recorded amendments and the real system is the operator's memory again - now with false confidence attached

failure_modes: discovering an auto-renew after its notice window closed
a verbal promise of near-perfect uptime that the upstream SLA never supported
computing an outage credit against terms nobody can find
acceptance_tests: every active account has a register entry with term dates, notice window, rate mechanics, hardware ownership, and the SLA basis naming its upstream source document
no customer-facing availability promise exceeds the recorded upstream SLA basis
revisit_triggers: any amendment, renewal, or upstream SLA revision
a credit calculation or entitlement question the register cannot answer

base.update_signal: an amendment, upstream SLA change, or register miss during a live credit or renewal question

nodes.definition: Conduct renewals on disclosure: give proactive notice ahead of the auto-renew window even where the contract would let the term roll silently, open with a review of what the account actually uses so the renewed contract matches reality rather than perpetuating stale seat counts, and quote at current honest pricing with any change explained as mechanism - wholesale moved, support load changed, feature mix changed - never as a theatrical expiring discount. No evergreen traps: no multi-year rollover buried in silence, no rate jump smuggled past the notice date, no renewal terms the customer discovers rather than accepts. The commercial logic is that a renewal earned by service and disclosure holds for its full term, while one captured by fine print churns with resentment at the first legal opening and invites the complaint-and-dispute class of trouble that follows evergreen-trap conduct. The renewal conversation is also the natural moment the account's grievances surface while there is still time to fix them.

included: proactive pre-window notice
re-verified seats and mechanism-explained pricing
the no-evergreen-trap rule
excluded: initial contract design
the account review that ideally precedes the renewal conversation

pros.claim: Pre-notice renewal conversations surface fixable grievances while there is still time
pros.example: a restaurant's renewal call unearths a six-month-old voicemail-to-email fault; fixing it wins a two-year renewal that a silent rollover would have lost angrily at the next opening

cons.claim: Proactively opening renewals invites shopping that silence would not have
cons.example: an office manager reminded of the renewal date collects two competing quotes she would never have sought unprompted

failure_modes: silent auto-renewals customers discover angrily
renewing stale seat counts and re-signing the account to an invoice it already resents
dressing an ordinary re-quote as a fake expiring discount
acceptance_tests: every renewal in the log shows notice given before the window, seats re-verified against reality, and any price change explained by its mechanism in writing
revisit_triggers: a renewal-window miss or a renewal dispute
wholesale or contract-mechanics changes that alter what honest renewal pricing looks like

base.update_signal: renewal outcomes show the proactive motion losing accounts silence would have kept, or vice versa

nodes.definition: Run periodic account reviews as a service artifact, not a sales ambush: the agenda is drawn from the account's own record - ticket history and repeat faults, quality trends, seat count against current headcount, features paid for against features used, upcoming contract dates from the register, and any E911-relevant changes such as moves, new rooms, or remote users - with cadence set by tier rather than uniformly. The honest outputs are exactly four: all good, fix something, right-size in either direction, or a genuine expansion or cross-sell need the customer recognizes as their own once shown the evidence. The review earns the right to sell by first proving the operator reads the account; the moment reviews become pitches, customers stop taking them, and the operator loses the single best structured look at each account's health, compliance posture, and growth surface.

included: the record-driven agenda
tier-set cadence
the four honest outputs
excluded: executing the expansion or cross-sell the review surfaces
the tiering that sets the cadence

pros.claim: Review-sourced expansion converts without pressure because the customer sees their own data
pros.example: a review showing a trucking office's after-hours calls dying in a general voicemail leads the owner to ask for the ring-group and mobile-app change himself

cons.claim: Reviews across a whole book are hours of unbilled preparation
cons.example: prepping usage and ticket summaries for thirty accounts each quarter competes directly with fault work and installs

failure_modes: turning the review into a pitch and losing the trust that makes reviews welcome
canned agendas that ignore the account's record and teach the customer reviews are skippable
skipping reviews for small accounts entirely until their first contact in a year is the renewal notice
acceptance_tests: each completed review shows an agenda built from that account's record and closes with one of the four honest outputs logged with a next action
revisit_triggers: review outputs cluster on all-good while churn continues - the agenda is missing what matters
tier changes that alter the owed cadence
customers declining reviews, signaling they have started to feel like pitches

base.update_signal: review outcomes stop correlating with retention and expansion, or customers begin declining them

nodes.definition: Grow MRR from inside the book, where it is cheapest: no acquisition cost, no port risk, no unknown network. Detect expansion moments from the account's own life - a new hire, an added operatory or truck, a second location, a seasonal ramp - mostly surfaced by reviews and support contact, then quote the add cleanly under the contracted rate mechanics and provision it with the same discipline as a miniature deployment: device or softphone configured, call-flow placement decided, the E911 dispatchable-location record created and verified for every new seat before the ticket closes, the contract register updated, and the change appearing on the next invoice. Seasonal verticals ramp both directions: a motel that adds seats for summer will ask to drop them in winter, and handling the down-ramp gracefully under contracted seasonal mechanics is precisely what makes the up-ramp come back every spring instead of going to a competitor who promises not to argue about it.

included: expansion-moment detection
clean quoting under contracted mechanics
miniature-deployment provisioning with the E911 record per new seat
excluded: new-logo acquisition
full new-site deployments, which route back to the deployment discipline

pros.claim: Existing-account seat growth is the cheapest MRR the business ever earns
pros.example: a dental practice adding two operatories takes two phones, an afternoon, and zero acquisition spend - against weeks of selling to win an equivalent new account

cons.claim: Treating every seasonal down-ramp as a fight poisons the relationship the up-ramp depends on
cons.example: arguing a motel out of its winter seat reduction wins one quarter of MRR and loses the account by the following summer

failure_modes: adding seats without their E911 records and discovering the gap in an audit or an emergency
quoting adds ad hoc instead of under the contracted mechanics, creating invoice disputes
expansion work skipping the register and invoice so records drift from reality
acceptance_tests: every seat add closes with device configured, call-flow placement done, E911 record verified, register updated, and the change on the next invoice
revisit_triggers: an account opens a location or crosses into needs the current platform tier cannot serve
seasonal patterns shift, changing when ramp conversations are owed

base.update_signal: expansion tickets repeatedly miss a checklist item, or growth stalls while reviews show unserved expansion moments

nodes.definition: Sell features off the account's own evidence, then make them stick. The ticket log and review data reveal what to offer: missed-call complaints at a dental front desk point at call queues or answering overflow; a restaurant drowning in are-you-open calls points at an hours-and-directions attendant and text auto-reply where the platform supports it; trucking dispatch friction points at mobile apps and ring groups; a motel's front desk points at wake-up and room-status features the platform actually provides. The observed need is named to the customer as the reason for the offer - which is what separates service from quota-selling - and no feature is ever pitched because a platform spiff or a revenue target says so. Adoption mechanics matter as much as the sale: every feature add includes setup, a short training touch, and a check at the next contact that it is actually used, because an activated-but-unused feature is a line item the customer resents at every invoice and a ready-made grievance at renewal.

included: mapping observed pain to platform features by vertical
naming the evidence in the offer
adoption follow-through: setup, training touch, usage check
excluded: adjacent non-phone services - the cross-sell boundary governs those
inventing feature uptake or revenue figures

pros.claim: Evidence-named feature offers convert as service rather than selling
pros.example: showing a dentist eleven missed calls over two lunch hours makes the overflow-answering feature her idea by the end of the sentence

cons.claim: Per-add feature revenue is small against the setup and training labor honesty demands
cons.example: chasing a dozen tiny feature adds across the book can cost more crew hours in setup and follow-through than the added MRR covers for months

failure_modes: pitching features on quota or platform spiff rather than observed need
activating features without the training touch so they go unused and curdle into renewal grievances
offering a feature the platform technically lists but delivers poorly for this vertical
acceptance_tests: every feature offer in the log names the observed evidence behind it, and every add shows the setup, training touch, and a later usage check
revisit_triggers: usage checks show a feature class going unused after adoption - the offer map or training is wrong
the platform adds, changes, or sunsets features relevant to the book's verticals

base.update_signal: adoption checks or platform feature changes invalidate part of the vertical-to-feature map

nodes.definition: Cross-sell adjacent services - business internet, cameras, Wi-Fi, cabling - only inside three honest limits. First, capability: offer only what the operator can genuinely deliver and support, or transparently broker with full disclosure of who delivers and who supports what; a camera system sold and abandoned poisons the phone relationship that funds everything. Second, provenance: the offer must arise from a finding in the account's own review or service history - dead Wi-Fi zones discovered while triaging a phone fault, an internet contract expiring at a motel, a break-in next door raising camera interest - never from a quota or a distributor promotion. Third, independence: never leverage support dependence to move unrelated product, and a declined cross-sell changes nothing about service quality, stated explicitly when declining customers seem to worry otherwise. Done inside the limits, adjacency deepens the moat because one trusted local vendor is genuinely convenient; overreach converts a trusted phone specialist into a distrusted everything-peddler, and the trust does not come back at the next renewal.

included: the capability, provenance, and independence limits
disclosure of broker roles
the explicit no-consequence statement for declined offers
excluded: the engineering of the adjacent services themselves
phone-platform feature upsell, which has its own node

pros.claim: Boundaried adjacency deepens the moat around the phone relationship
pros.example: a motel that buys honestly delivered Wi-Fi from its phone operator now has two services it would need to migrate, and a vendor it trusts with both

cons.claim: The boundary forgoes real revenue the operator could technically close today
cons.example: declining to resell a camera system the operator cannot support leaves a signed-ready deal on the table for a competitor to take

failure_modes: selling adjacency the operator cannot support and burning the core phone trust
quota-driven cross-sell pitches that teach customers every review hides an agenda
undisclosed broker arrangements the customer discovers at the first service failure
acceptance_tests: every cross-sell offer traces to a named review or service finding, states who delivers and who supports, and declined offers show no change in the account's service record
revisit_triggers: the operator's genuine delivery capability changes in either direction
a supported adjacent service generates ticket load the phone margin quietly subsidizes

base.update_signal: delivery capability, broker arrangements, or evidence that cross-sold services are eroding core-service trust

nodes.definition: Understand the book's economics as mechanisms whose actual numbers come from the operator's own records, never from asserted industry figures: account margin is contracted per-seat retail minus platform wholesale minus allocated support labor minus billing and payment costs, with each input living in a named place - the customer contract, the upstream agreement, the time log, the processor statement. Book MRR is the sum across accounts, and its month-over-month motion decomposes into new accounts, expansion, contraction from right-sizing, and churn - tracking the four separately is what turns a vague good-month feeling into a diagnosis. Retention compounds because a kept account pays its margin every month with no new acquisition cost and keeps its referral surface alive, while a churned account removes both at once. The mechanism also exposes the quiet failure: support-heavy accounts can run negative real margin invisibly until labor is allocated, even coarsely - which is why the time log, however rough, is a required input and not bookkeeping perfectionism.

included: the margin mechanism with named input sources
the four-way MRR motion decomposition
coarse labor allocation as a required input
excluded: asserting any specific margin, multiple, or churn figure
the load-reduction actions the analysis motivates

pros.claim: Even coarse labor allocation exposes accounts whose real margin is negative
pros.example: a rough time log reveals two of the book's smallest accounts consuming a third of all support hours - invisible in every revenue-only view of the book

cons.claim: Margin math on coarse tracking misjudges individual accounts on small samples
cons.example: one quarter containing a single brutal fault makes a fundamentally good restaurant account look margin-negative and invites a wrong re-price conversation

failure_modes: running the book on revenue alone while support labor silently inverts the margin on particular accounts
lumping the four MRR motions together so churn hides inside expansion
importing a plausible-sounding industry figure instead of computing from the operator's own records
acceptance_tests: the book worksheet computes each account's margin from inputs traced to their named source records, and monthly MRR motion is decomposed into the four components
revisit_triggers: wholesale terms, processor costs, or crew wages change any input
an account's allocated labor contradicts its perceived health in either direction

base.update_signal: any margin input's source changes, or the decomposition reveals a motion the mechanism cannot explain

nodes.definition: Manage the labor side of book margin by attacking causes instead of absorbing touches: review ticket causes periodically to find the repeat drivers - one router model behind half the quality complaints across accounts, one auto-attendant that customers cannot edit themselves, one training gap producing the same voicemail question weekly - and prefer the permanent fix over the cheap repeat touch, because at book scale the repeat touch is the more expensive path. Build the self-service layer deliberately: one-page quick guides per vertical, one trained admin contact per account who handles greetings and simple changes, portal how-tos for the changes customers ask for most. Keep as-builts current so no fault begins with rediscovery. When one account's load stays high after the fixes and the training, the finding routes to an honest conversation - an architecture fix quoted as project work, a scope reset against the charter, or a re-price under the contracted mechanics - never to silent absorption that breeds resentment or silent service degradation that breeds churn.

included: repeat-cause review and permanent fixes
the self-service layer and trained admin contacts
the honest routing of persistent load outliers
excluded: the charter that defines bundled scope
individual fault triage mechanics

pros.claim: One permanent fix retires an entire ticket class across the book
pros.example: replacing the one router model with broken SIP handling at the four accounts that have it ends a quality-complaint stream that consumed hours every month

cons.claim: Permanent fixes and guide-building cost unpaid hours now for savings that arrive later
cons.example: an afternoon writing the motel front-desk quick guide produces nothing billable that week, and its payoff is invisible except as calls that never happen

failure_modes: absorbing repeat touches indefinitely because each one is individually small
silently resenting a heavy account instead of running the honest re-price or scope conversation
letting as-builts drift so every fault re-pays the rediscovery tax
acceptance_tests: the periodic cause review exists with dated findings, each top repeat driver has a permanent-fix decision, and every persistent load outlier shows a documented conversation outcome rather than silent absorption
revisit_triggers: ticket volume or causes shift after platform updates or new device classes
a load outlier's conversation outcome fails to actually reduce the load

base.update_signal: the cause mix shifts or a fix class stops retiring its ticket stream

nodes.definition: Tier the book on stated facts so finite attention lands where it earns, while the floors stay uniform because they are obligations, not privileges. Tier inputs: revenue weight (share of book MRR), strategic weight (referenceable accounts in a vertical - the dental office other dentists ask, the motel owner who knows every motel owner in the county), health (open flags and their severity), and support load. The tier sets what may legitimately vary: review cadence and depth, proactive monitoring attention, expansion effort, and who gets the first call in a multi-account incident. What may never vary by tier: response within the sold support promise, E911 record discipline, billing integrity, and renewal disclosure - degrading any of those for small accounts is both a promise breach and, for the compliance floor, not the operator's to waive. Tiering exists precisely so the operator can be honest about attention instead of pretending every account gets prime treatment while quietly triaging by gut.

included: the four tier inputs
what tier may vary versus the uniform floors
attention allocation in multi-account incidents
excluded: the review agendas the tier schedules
the economics computation feeding the revenue weight

pros.claim: Explicit tiering replaces gut-feel triage with defensible attention allocation
pros.example: in a platform incident, calling the three-property motel account first is a written rule rather than a panicked judgment call made differently each time

cons.claim: Tier labels can quietly ossify into self-fulfilling neglect of the bottom tier
cons.example: a small law office parked in the lowest tier stops getting reviews entirely, and its first meaningful contact in a year is the renewal notice it declines

failure_modes: letting tiers erode the floors so small accounts get slower-than-promised response
tiering on revenue alone and missing the strategically referenceable small account
never re-tiering so last year's map allocates this year's attention
acceptance_tests: every account carries a tier derived from the four stated inputs, and a floor check confirms response, E911, billing, and renewal conduct do not vary by tier
revisit_triggers: an account's MRR, health, load, or strategic weight changes materially
the book gate finds attention flowing contrary to the tier map

base.update_signal: material change in any account's tier inputs, or floor checks failing on lower tiers

nodes.definition: Treat the upstream platform as the concentration risk the entire book stands on, and watch it like one: track wholesale price changes and the operator's own upstream agreement terms and renewal dates; log every incident with date, scope, duration, and the platform's handling, because the log - not the memory of the last bad week - is the evidence for a hard negotiation or a migration decision; watch the feature roadmap against what the book's verticals keep asking for, support responsiveness trends on escalated tickets, and visible signals of the platform's own business health. Maintain a standing rough answer to what moving the book would cost - porting every account's numbers at scale, re-provisioning devices, retraining customers, contract friction on both sides - because a credible migration option is the only real leverage a reseller holds over its platform. The mechanism for keeping the option honest is a small second-platform lane: a pilot with a few new accounts proves the alternative works before the day the whole book needs it, and its existence changes the tone of every wholesale renewal conversation.

included: the incident log as decision evidence
wholesale terms and roadmap watch
the costed migration option and second-platform pilot lane
excluded: executing a book migration - that becomes a deployment-scale program
individual escalation mechanics

pros.claim: A credible, piloted migration option converts the reseller from captive to counterparty
pros.example: walking into a wholesale renewal with a dated incident log and three accounts already running clean on an alternative platform changes what the platform offers before the conversation starts

cons.claim: A second-platform lane doubles the surface the operator must master and support
cons.example: two portals, two provisioning flows, and two escalation paths for a one-person shop means every runbook and training artifact now exists twice

failure_modes: discovering platform decline only when accounts start churning over quality the operator cannot fix
deciding stay-or-go from the latest incident instead of the log
keeping a theoretical migration option that has never been piloted and collapses under its first real test
acceptance_tests: the platform file holds the current upstream terms and renewal date, a dated incident log, and a refreshed rough migration costing
the migration option is backed by at least a small live pilot or an explicit dated decision not to run one
revisit_triggers: any upstream price, term, or ownership change
an incident-frequency trend crossing what the book's SLAs can absorb
the pilot platform outperforming or underperforming the primary in a way that shifts the calculus

base.update_signal: upstream terms, incident trend, platform ownership, or pilot results materially change

nodes.definition: Close the loop with a periodic whole-book review - quarterly fits most small books - that composes everything upstream into dated decisions with owners, so book management is an operated loop rather than a mood. The gate walks the book: open churn flags become save actions or accepted exits with reasons; contracts entering their notice windows next quarter become scheduled honest-renewal conversations; review findings become expansion quotes or right-sizing actions within the cross-sell boundary; load outliers become fix, scope, or re-price conversations; and the platform file becomes an explicit continue, negotiate, or extend-the-pilot stance. The definition-of-done is per account: current health state, tier, verified contract dates, E911 records confirmed current, and a next action - or a written exception with a reason and a date. Accounts failing the definition are the gate's real output, because each one is a place where the book's records have quietly diverged from reality, and divergence is where churn, compliance failures, and billing disputes incubate unseen.

included: the composed walk of flags, windows, findings, outliers, and platform stance
the per-account definition-of-done
dated decisions with owners
excluded: executing the decisions - each routes to its owning node
the per-account review sessions themselves

pros.claim: The gate surfaces record-reality divergence before it becomes churn or compliance failure
pros.example: a quarterly walk finds an account whose contract renewed unrecorded and whose office moved without an E911 update - two incubating failures caught in one sitting

cons.claim: A full-book gate is a heavy sitting a solo operator is tempted to skip in a busy quarter
cons.example: skipping one quarter's gate feels free until the next one finds two closed notice windows and a stale platform file

failure_modes: running the gate as a glance instead of a walk so exceptions pile up undated
decisions logged without owners and dates, evaporating by the next quarter
skipping the gate in busy quarters - exactly when divergence accumulates fastest
acceptance_tests: each gate pass logs, for every account, either the full definition-of-done or a written exception with reason and date, and every decision names an owner and a date
revisit_triggers: gate findings repeat unresolved across passes, meaning decisions are not executing
book size or crew changes make the cadence too heavy or too thin

base.update_signal: gate passes stop catching divergence that later surfaces as churn, compliance, or billing incidents

edges.why_related: the intake record exists to serve the book the frame defines - what support must hold follows from what the recurring stage is
the support charter is written against what was actually deployed and promised, both of which live in the intake record
triage operates inside the charter's hours, channels, and response bands
the local layers are ruled out and the evidence captured before any upstream ticket opens
outage handling builds on the escalation discipline - the same upstream channels and evidence habits, run at whole-book blast radius
continuing E911 maintenance starts from the dispatchable-location records as registered at cutover, which the intake record carries
billing hygiene implements the bill-honestly job of the book and inherits the channel-model position the frame carries forward
ticket-pattern signals are only readable against the charter's definition of normal support traffic
payment slippage and disputed invoices are health signals that come straight out of the billing cycle
the save motion fires on flags - without signal reading, saves happen only at the cancellation call, too late
the register is seeded from the contract, promise, and hardware-ownership facts the intake record delivers
renewal timing and honest quoting both read directly from the register's dates, notice windows, and rate mechanics
the tier sets each account's review cadence and depth
reviews are the structured surface where expansion moments are detected and quoted honestly
the review's usage-versus-paid and ticket-pattern evidence is what a legitimate feature offer is built from
the boundary's provenance rule requires a review or service finding behind every adjacency offer
the revenue and load weights that drive tiering come out of the book economics worksheet
labor allocation identifies which repeat causes and which accounts are worth permanent-fix and conversation effort
escalation outcomes and responsiveness trends are primary entries in the platform file
the gate walks the book in tier order and checks attention against the tier map
the gate schedules the coming quarter's renewal conversations from the notice-window forward look
each gate pass closes with an explicit platform stance read from the platform file
the account review runs before the renewal conversation so the renewal opens with grievances already surfaced and seats already verified
outage communication and credits are bounded by the SLA terms the register records - nothing stronger may be promised mid-incident
a feature may only be sold if its ongoing support burden fits inside the charter the fee funds
an expansion is not complete until the add lands accurately on the next invoice - billing hygiene gates the growth motion's closure
the gate may approve cross-sell actions only when they satisfy the capability, provenance, and independence limits
the save instinct wants time and friction exactly where the exit duty demands prompt cooperation
edges.resolution_rule: once porting data is requested, offboarding duties win absolutely - porting information goes out promptly and any remaining save runs only as an honest parallel conversation, never as delay

edges.why_related: every feature sold adds configuration surface and future ticket load to the exact budget load control is trying to shrink
edges.resolution_rule: an offer whose projected support burden exceeds what the bundled charter absorbs is sold with setup and training included or not sold; for accounts already flagged as load outliers, load control wins outright

edges.why_related: book-growth pressure pushes toward closing every adjacent deal the boundary exists to filter
edges.resolution_rule: the boundary wins whenever the offer's trigger is a revenue target rather than a review finding - adjacency revenue is forgone before core-service trust is spent

edges.why_related: same-day seat adds and moves push for speed that the record discipline deliberately slows
edges.resolution_rule: E911 wins without exception - a seat is not delivered until its dispatchable-location record is verified; speed is recovered by parallelizing provisioning, never by skipping the record

edges.why_related: a save under pressure wants to bend the bundled line that the charter exists to hold
edges.resolution_rule: the line may bend only as a documented exception with an expiry date - never as silent precedent; for the top tier the exception is granted readily, for the rest the charter holds

edges.why_related: unresolved and repeating faults are the direct generators of the ticket-pattern churn flags
billing surprises are among the most common causes of the save conversations the playbook ends up running
every handled incident produces the dated log entry that accumulates into the stay-negotiate-migrate evidence
wholesale price and term changes caught by the watch move the margin input of every account in the book at once
repeat-cause findings feed back into where the bundled-versus-billable line should actually be drawn
every executed renewal writes new terms, dates, and windows back into the register it was driven from
exit findings from departed accounts recalibrate which signals actually predicted the loss
both are review-sourced within-account growth motions sharing the same evidence-named offer discipline and adoption follow-through

conflict_axes.name: save_the_account_vs_respect_the_exit
conflict_axes.description: The retention instinct wants friction and time wherever a customer moves to leave, while the exit duty demands prompt, complete porting cooperation because the number belongs to the customer.
poles: fight for every account with every available day
honor the customer's right to leave frictionlessly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: saves run freely up to the moment porting data is requested; from that moment cooperation duties dominate and persuasion continues only in honest parallel

conflict_axes.name: bundled_generosity_vs_margin_protection
conflict_axes.description: Generous inclusion of support work builds the loyalty the book runs on, while every absorbed touch erodes the per-seat margin that makes the book worth running.
poles: hold the bundled line to protect margin
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: write the line, grant documented exceptions with expiry dates, and route chronic outliers to an honest scope or re-price conversation instead of silent absorption or silent resentment

conflict_axes.name: expansion_push_vs_earned_trust
conflict_axes.description: Growth pressure wants every review to produce an offer, while the review's value depends on customers believing it is service, not a pitch in disguise.
poles: protect the review as a trusted service artifact
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: offers are made only when the account's own record evidences the need and the evidence is named to the customer; a review with nothing to sell ends with nothing sold

conflict_axes.name: proactive_disclosure_vs_sleeping_dogs
conflict_axes.description: Disclosure-first conduct - renewal notices, outage notifications, unprompted credits - invites shopping and credit claims that silence would have avoided, but silence compounds into resentment and disputes.
poles: disclose proactively and absorb the short-term cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure wins; the shopping and claims it invites are the operating cost of a book that renews on trust rather than on inattention

conflict_axes.name: service_speed_vs_compliance_gating
conflict_axes.description: Customers measure the operator in same-day responsiveness, while the E911 record discipline deliberately holds tickets open until location records are verified.
poles: hold every ticket for its compliance action
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compliance wins without exception; speed is recovered by parallelizing the record work inside the ticket, never by skipping it

conflict_axes.name: operator_accountability_vs_platform_dependence
conflict_axes.description: The customer bought from the operator and holds the operator accountable, yet the fix for platform faults sits in an upstream organization the operator does not control.
poles: own every outcome as if the network were yours
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: own the communication, the evidence, and the escalation pressure completely; attribute the fix truthfully without hiding behind the carrier, and log every incident as future leverage

conflict_axes.name: account_level_attention_vs_book_level_efficiency
conflict_axes.description: Every account deserves prime treatment in principle, while a small crew's hours force attention to be rationed somewhere, acknowledged or not.
poles: treat every account as top tier
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tier the variable attention explicitly and keep the floors - response promise, E911, billing, renewal disclosure - uniform because they are obligations, not privileges

conflict_axes.name: mrr_growth_vs_right_sizing_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Every seat kept on the invoice grows MRR now, while seats the customer does not use are churn fuel accumulating interest.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: right-size first: an honestly smaller account compounds longer than an oversubscribed one survives, and the credibility earned makes the next expansion conversation easier

conflict_axes.name: fix_forever_vs_bill_the_touch
conflict_axes.description: A permanent fix costs unpaid hours now and removes future contact, while repeat touches are individually cheap, sometimes billable, and keep the operator visible.
poles: invest in permanent fixes and self-service
handle each touch as it comes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: when cause analysis shows recurrence, the permanent fix wins - at book scale the repeat touch is the more expensive path and the visibility it buys is the wrong kind

edge_cases.description: A customer's office floods overnight; the business must answer calls from a temporary location by morning and every E911 record for the site is suddenly wrong
edge_cases.trigger: sudden forced relocation of a served site
edge_cases.mitigation: activate emergency forwarding to cells immediately, update dispatchable-location records for wherever devices physically land the same day, and verify current requirements for the temporary-site situation rather than guessing

edge_cases.description: The platform announces a wholesale price increase that hits every account's margin at once, mid-way through most customers' contract terms
edge_cases.mitigation: recompute margins book-wide, check each contract's rate-change mechanics before touching any price, pass changes through only as disclosed mechanism at the contractually allowed moment, and never recover the difference through padded fee lines

edge_cases.description: A customer demands guaranteed one-hundred-percent uptime language as a renewal condition
edge_cases.trigger: an uptime guarantee request exceeding the verified basis
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the unsupported number; offer the upstream provider's published SLA as the availability basis plus the operator's own staffed response commitments, and document the exchange in the register

edge_cases.description: A served dental practice is sold and the new owner disputes both the contract and the auto-renew they never signed
edge_cases.mitigation: raise an ownership-change health flag, treat the transition as a re-earn and re-contract conversation rather than enforcing inherited fine print as leverage, and record the new agreement cleanly

edge_cases.description: An account files its third quality ticket in a month and then goes completely silent
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the silence itself as the alarm: proactive root-cause visit with the fault history in hand, fix confirmed before any commercial conversation, save logged either way

edge_cases.description: A port-out request arrives for an account that is mid-save and carries two unpaid invoices
edge_cases.trigger: exit initiated during an active save with a balance outstanding
edge_cases.mitigation: release accurate porting data promptly regardless; pursue the balance as ordinary collections on a separate track, keep any continuing save conversation honest and parallel, and verify current porting-rule obligations rather than testing them

edge_cases.description: A seasonal motel asks to drop two-thirds of its seats for the winter
edge_cases.trigger: seasonal contraction request in a hospitality account
